summary: The v38 mismatch is caused by the existing apply.c:set_trap caller skipping the C trap trigger. After a cursed bear trap is armed and rnl(10) exceeds 5, C calls dotrap(ttmp, 0); JS still records note_unported("trap.c dotrap") and skips the side effect. The trap effect itself is already implemented. B204 currently owns the complete dotrap implementation, so caller closure must wait for that delivery to be accepted.

source.branch: When the occupation finishes, a cursed bear trap or fumbling hero triggers the armed trap if rnl(10) > 5; force_bungle triggers it unconditionally. The return from dotrap is discarded, but its state and output side effects are required.
callers: apply.c:doapply selects the bear trap and calls use_trap.
allmain.c occupation processing invokes set_trap once per occupied turn.
apply.c:set_trap calls trap.c:dotrap after maketrap and arming messages; trap.c:dotrap dispatches the hero BEAR_TRAP to trapeffect_bear_trap.
dependencies: B204 delivery b163add4e236bfc3597f6ae5e596d194629fe5c5 owns source:trap.c:dotrap and its implementation in js/trap_effects.js; this caller cannot reach the completed callee until B204 is accepted.

evidence: The current queue reports the first mismatch at segment 0 step 43, key n: C RNG starts with d(2,4)=7 from trap.c:trapeffect_bear_trap; JS instead continues the monster turn with rn2(12)=7. The admitted case has 45 steps and two remaining screens.

The recorded step 43 C trace is rnl(10)=6 @ set_trap(apply.c:2941), rn2(5)=3 @ dotrap(trap.c:3038), d(2,4)=7 and rn2(4)=3 @ trapeffect_bear_trap. At step 44, C records the trap-close result and the recovery/exercise calls.
